messages.subject: cluster variable
parts:
Dear all,

I'm analyzing bilateral asymmetry using facial 3D images (object symmetry). 
I want to study the FA component using a regression model. The thing is that I need to incorporate a cluster variable. Does anybody know if there is any linear regression to analyze the FA component that allows the incorporation of a cluster variable? 

Thanks in advanced.

Best regards, 

Julia Ratowiecki
PhD Candidate
Universidad de Buenos Aires, Argentina.

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] cluster variable
parts:
Julia,

it is not clear to me what you mean by "incorporating a cluster variable". You can use the function bilat.symmetry to  first test for the presence of FA and then extract an individual asymmetry index for your data, which you could then analyse with respect to other explanatory variables (assuming this is what you are trying to do, i.e. ask whether FA varies as a response to this "cluster" you are talking about).

Hope this helps
Antigoni

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] cluster variable
parts:
Julia, 

I am sorry but from your description I cannot advise how to proceed, as I do not understand what you mean that "I have individuals from the same family and I want to adjust for it by adding "family" as a cluster."

If you are thinking about having family as a random factor in the Procrustes ANOVA that evaluates asymmetry parameters (i.e. individual, side, with replicates for measurement error etc) you would need to build this ANOVA model yourself using procD.lm. This is certainly possible. A look to the help file of procD.lm and (maybe more so) to the help and vignettes of lm.rrpp in the RRPP package, would help.

But if what you want is to compare FA levels across families that is a whole different story. In that case, I would first run bilat.symmetry, then extract individual asymmetry indices (and if you want the asymmetric shape component, although I am not completely sure what a comparison of that component might tell you biologically) and then use lm.rrpp to run a model with level of asymmetry as the response variable, and family as the predictor.

Antigoni
